result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B fits the rubric better: it limits color to exceptions, keeps every row dense and the same height, and lines numbers up with tabular numerals, so normal rows stay quiet. A puts a green/amber/red bar on every row and gives exceptions bigger type, which adds visual noise. Both reject the hero stat in favor of a thin strip and respond to the user's idea, though A goes softer on the bigger-cards idea and B says the alert count could be shown big. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn down the hero stat and big cards in favour of a slim summary strip and a layout split by where each truck is. A sticks more closely to quiet, uniform rows: it uses colour only for exceptions, keeps status as a neutral label, and is honest about the height limit. B weakens that by adding green/amber/red minute bars to every row and enlarging exception rows, which brings back loudness and size differences.
